away.name: Arturs Silovs
away.news: Sergei Murashov had a decent outing in his season debut last game, but the team will turn to Silovs to start for the third time in four games to start the season. The 25-year-old Silovs was outstanding in his season opener, saving all 19 shots he faced in a 7-0 win over the Philadelphia Flyers, but was not nearly as dominant in his following outing, allowing five goals on 25 shots (.800 SV%) while managing to salvage a 6-5 overtime victory over the Montreal Canadiens. The Penguins enter Wednesday's contest as +139 road underdogs against a Washington Capitals team that is 1-1-0 this season.

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Thompson has quietly become one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies over the past several seasons, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. The 29-year-old goalie hopes to continue his upward trajectory after an encouraging start to the season, saving 31 of 33 shots (.939 SV%) in his only game so far, a 5-2 win over the Carolina Hurricanes. The Capitals enter Wednesday as -154 home favourites against a Pittsburgh Penguins team that has outscored its opposition 15-8 through three games (2-1-0).

away.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
away.news: To some surprise, Colorado hasn't yet turned to Scott Wedgewood this season and will roll with Blackwood between the pipes for a third straight game. Despite Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, it's hard to blame Head Coach Jared Bednar for turning to Blackwood again, given his solid 2.50 GAA and .912 SV% through the first two games (2-0-0). Colorado enters Wednesday's contest as sizeable -193 road favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that is 2-0-1 this season.

home.name: Stuart Skinner
home.news: Skinner will start Wednesday vs. the Avalanche.

away.name: Devon Levi
away.news: Levi has been far from spectacular, but he has won both of his outings and will return to the crease for a third straight game on Wednesday against the Anaheim Ducks. The 24-year-old goalie has a chance to earn significant playing time in Edmonton, but he certainly hopes to improve his 4.02 GAA and .810 SV% over his two games this season (2-0-0).

home.name: Lukas Dostal
home.news: With Ville Husso as his backup, the Ducks will likely rely heavily on Dostal, who returns to the crease Wednesday against the Edmonton Oilers. The 26-year-old Dostal has played both games for the Ducks this season (2-0-0), posting a solid 2.42 GAA and .918 SV%. It will be his first time facing the Oilers since helping eliminate them from last postseason in six games. The Ducks enter Wednesday's contest as +116 home underdogs against the Oilers, who have scored 17 goals in their first three games (2-0-1).
